la:adj:obscurus.html:
obscūrus, a, um, adj.
Sanscr. sku, to cover, akin to Gr. σκευή, σκῦτος, κύτος; cf.: scutum, cutis
,
dark, darksome, dusky, shady, obscure (class.).
Lit.: unde (Acherunte) animae excitantur obscurā umbrā, in dark, shadowy forms, Poët. ap. ; so, umbra,: donec in obscurum coni conduxit acumen,the obscure point of the cone,: lucus,: antrum,: convalles,: tabernae,; cf. : aliae res obnoxiosae nocte in obscurā latent, Enn. ap. (17), 10 (Trag. v. 341 Vahl.): nox,; cf.: per occasum solis, jam obscurā luce,: caelum,: nimbus,: nubes,: ferrugo,i. e. black,: dentes,.—Poet.: funda, dark, i. e. invisible, ; cf. mamma,i. e. hidden, covered,: aquae,i. e. turbid,.—Subst.: obscūrum, i, n., dim light, twilight: in obscuro, advesperascente die,; but commonly the dark, darkness, obscurity: sub obscurum noctis,: lumen,i. e. darkness visible,.—obscū-rum, adverb.: obscurum nimbosus dissidet aër,.—
Transf., to the person who is in the dark, darkling, unseen: ibant obscuri solā sub nocte per umbram,: obscurus in ulvā Delitui,.—
Trop.
In gen., dark, obscure, indistinct, unintelligible: Heraclitus ... Clarus ob obscuram linguam,: valde Heraclitus obscurus (cf. the Gr. appellation of Heraclitus, ὁ σκοτεινός), : quid? poëta nemo, nemo physicus obscurus?: obscurā de re tam lucida pango carmina,; : brevis esse laboro, Obscurus fio,: reperta Graiorum,: obscurum et ignotum jus,: cur hoc tam est obscurum atque caecum?: nolo plebem Romanam obscurā spe et caecā expectatione haerere,uncertain,.—Comp., .—Sup.: videre res obscurissimas,.—Subst.: causae in obscuro positae,—
In partic., rhet. t. t.: obscurum genus causae, obscure, i. e. intricate, involved, Gr. δυσπαρακολούθητον, : (causae privatae) sunt multo saepe obscuriores,.—
Not known, unknown, not recognized: forma,: P Ilas,i. e. disguised, under another form,.—Esp. of rank and station, obscure, ignoble, mean, low: non est obscura tua in me benevolentia,: Caesaris in barbaris erat nomen obscurius, * : Pompeius humili atque obscuro loco natus,of an obscure, ignoble family,: obscuris orti majoribus,from obscure ancestors,: clarus an obscurus,; cf.: si nobilis obscurum se vocet,; : non obscurus professor et auctor,: natus haud obscuro loco,.— Neutr. absol.: in obscuro vitam habere,: vitam per obscurum transmittere,in obscurity,: saepe mandatum initio litis in obscuro est,kept back,.—
Of character, close, secret, reserved: obscurus et astutus homo, (for which: sin me astutum et occultum lubet fingere,): plerumque modestus Occupat obscuri speciem,: Tiberium obscurum adversus alios, sibi uni incautum intectumque efficeret,: obscurum odium,.—Comp.: natura obscurior,.—Adv.: ob-scūrē, darkly, obscurely (class.).
Lit.: aut nihil superum aut obscure admodum cernimus, very darkly, ap. .—
Trop.
Of speech, darkly, obscurely, indistinctly: dicta,; .—Comp.: quae causa dicta obscurius est,.—Sup.: obscurissime particulā uti, Cell. 17, 13, 5: non obscurissime dicere (opp. planissime),.—
Of birth, obscurely, ignobly, meanly (perh. only post-class.): obscure natus,: obscurissime natus,.—
Covertly, closely, secretly: malum obscure serpens,: tacite obscureque perire,: non obscure ferre aliquid,; cf. ; .—Comp.: ceteri sunt obscurius iniqui,more secretly,, b, 2.—Sup.: avertere aliquid de publico quam obscurissime,.

la:verb:observo.gloss: to observe, watch, pay attention to
senses: to observe, watch, pay attention to
la:verb:observo.html:
ob-servo, āvi, ātum, 1 (archaic
fut. perf. observasso, ), v. a.
In gen., to watch, note, heed, observe a thing; to take notice of, pay attention to (class.; syn.: animadverto, attendo): ne me observare possis, quid rerum geram,: quid ille faciat, ne id observes,: fetus,to watch for, seek to catch,: lupus observavit, dum dormitarent canes,watched, waited,: occupationem alicujus, et aucupari tempus,to watch in order to take advantage of,: si iniquitates observaveris, Domine,: tempus epistulae alicui reddendae, to watch or wait for, : et insidiari,to be on the watch,: observavit sedulo, ut praetor indiceret, etc., took care that, etc., .—So pass. impers.: observatum est, ne quotiens introiret urbem, supplicium de quoquam sumeretur,: observans Acerroniae necem,observing, perceiving,: postquam poëta sensit, scripturam suam Ab iniquis observari,to be scrutinized,: sese,to keep a close watch over one's self,.—
In partic.
To watch, guard, keep any thing: januam,: fores,: greges,: draconem, auriferam obtutu observantem arborem, Poët. ap. ; .—
To observe, respect, regard, attend to, heed, keep, comply with a law, precept, recommendation, etc.: leges,: censoriam animadversionem,: praeceptum diligentissime,: imperium,: foedus,: centesimas,to adhere to,: commendationes,to attend to, regard,: auspicia,: diem concilii,: ordines,to keep in the ranks,.—Pass.: id ab omnibus,.—
To pay attention or respect to; to respect, regard, esteem, honor one (syn.: veneror, revereor): tribules suos,: regem,: me, ut alterum patrem, et observat, et diligit,: et colere aliquem,: aliquem perofficiose et amanter,: clarissimus et nobis observandus vir,.—
Observare se a quā re = se abstinere, .—
To observe, notice, perceive (eccl. Lat.): Amasa non observavit gladium,.—Hence,
ob-servans, antis, P. a.
Watchful, regardful, observant.—Comp.: observantior aequi Fit populus,.—Sup.: observantissimus omnium officiorum,; : observantissima lex suorum itinerum, App. de Mundo, 33 fin.—
Attentive, respectful: homo tui observans,; P.: observantissimus mei homo,; —Hence, adv.: observanter, carefully, sedulously (post-class.): sequi,; .—Comp.: observantius,.—Sup.: aliquid observantissime vitare,.—
Reverentially: ad precandum accedere,.—
observātē, adv., observantly, carefully, perspicaciously (postclass.): observate curioseque animadvertit M. Tullius,.

la:verb:obsum.gloss: to be against, be prejudicial to, be opposed to
senses: to be against, be prejudicial to, be opposed to
to hinder, get or be in the way
to hurt, injure, do harm to
la:verb:obsum.html:
ob-sum, obfui or offui, obesse (old form of
fut. obescet, oberit vel aderit, Paul. ex Müll.), v. n., to be against, be prejudicial to; to hinder, hurt, injure; opp. to prodesse (cf.: officio, noceo, injuriam facio; class.): Ty. Nunc falsa prosunt. Heg. At tibi oberunt, ; ; cf.: men obesse, illos prodesse, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 84 Vahl.); and: qui (pudor) non modo non obesset ejus orationi, sed etiam probitatis commendatione prodesset,: subicimus id. quod nobis adjumento futurum sit, aut offuturum illis e contrario. : obsunt auctoribus artes,: ne prodigus obsit,.—With a subject-clause: nec, dum degrandinat, obsit Agresti fano supposuisse pecus,: nihil obest dicere,.
la:verb:obsum.inflection: obfui or offui, obesse, v. n.

la:verb:obsecro.gloss: to entreat, implore, beseech, supplicate, beg, pray
senses: to entreat, implore, beseech, supplicate, beg, pray
la:verb:obsecro.html:
ob-sĕcro (op-sĕcro), āvi, ātum, 1 (separate, ob vos sacro, for vos obsecro, Paul. ex , Müll.), v. a.
sacro
, qs. to ask on religious grounds (ob sacrum), i. e.
to beseech, entreat, implore, supplicate, conjure: obsecrare est opem a sacris petere, Paul. ex Müll. (class.; syn.: obtestor, precor, supplico).—With acc. of the pers. or thing: Venus alma, ambae te obsecramus, Nos in custodiam tuam ut recipias,: advorsum quam ejus me opsecravisset pater,: cum eum oraret atque obsecraret,: te obsecrat obtestaturque per senectutem suam,conjures you,; : cum precibus me obsecraret, Marcell. ap. : cum multis lacrimis,; cf. in the foll.: pro di immortales, obsecro vostram fidem,; ; ; cf. in the foll.—
With a double acc. (of the pers. and thing): itaque te hoc obsecrat, ut,: hoc te,.—
With a relative or intentional clause: ut huc reveniat obsecrato,: pater, obsecro, ut mihi ignoscas,: te ut omnia perscribas, Cic. ; : ut ne,.—
Absol.: videmus certis precationibus obsecrasse summos magistratus,: Bassus multis precibus, paene etiam lacrimis obsecrabat, implerem meum tempus,: pro aliquo,; .—
In partic., in colloq. lang., obsecro.
As an expression of deprecation, I beseech you, I cry you mercy, for Heaven's sake: tuam fidem obsecro,: periimus! Obsecro hercle,: Ph. Prodi, male conciliate. Do. Obsecro, .—
As a mere polite expression of entreaty, for the most part as an interjection, I beseech you, pray: quid illic, opsecro, tam diu restitisti,; : dic obsecro hercle serio quod te rogem,; Turp. ap. : obsecro, an is est?: Attica mea, obsecro te, quid agit?; : sed obsecro te, ita venusta habeantur ista, non ut vincula virorum sint, sed, etc.,but I beseech you,; ; ; .

la:other:obsecro.gloss: please, I ask you, pray tell, prithee
senses: please, I ask you, pray tell, prithee
for God's sake, I'm begging you, for the love of God (an expression of exasperation)
la:other:obsecro.html:
ob-sĕcro (op-sĕcro), āvi, ātum, 1 (separate, ob vos sacro, for vos obsecro, Paul. ex , Müll.), v. a.

la:noun:obsignator.html:
obsignātor, ōris, m.
id.
,
a sealer, sealer up (class.): litterarum obsignator,.—Esp., the witnesses who set their seals to a will, : testamenti, 18, b, 2: decisionis,.

la:verb:obsigno.gloss: to seal up; to affix a seal to
senses: to seal up; to affix a seal to
to pledge or mortgage under hand and seal
la:verb:obsigno.html:
ob-signo, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. a., to seal, seal up a will, a letter, etc. (class.).
Lit.
In gen.: cedo tu ceram ac linum actutum: age obliga, obsigna cito,: cellas,: lagenas,: epistulam,; .—Esp.: tabulas, testamenta, to sign and seal, as a witness: istam ipsam quaestionem, dicite, quis obsignavit?: tabellas ejus rei condicionisque,: testamentum signis adulterinis,: obsignavit anulo,.—Prov.: agere cum aliquo tabellis obsignatis, to deal with one with sealed writings, i. e. in the strictest form, (cf.: tamquam ex syngraphā agere cum populo,): tabulas obsignare velle, would seal up the documents, i. e. would have no discussion, .—
In partic.
To seal up the papers and effects of an accused person, .—Hence,
To seal an accusation against one: qui contra Scaurum patrem suum obsignaverat, Fragm. ap. Ascon.—
To pledge or mortgage under one's hand and seal: tria agri jugera ad aerarium obsignaverat,.—
To close under seal, make fast: inane obsignari nihil solere,; cf. the context.—
Trop., to stamp, impress: formam verbi,: aliquid obsignatum habere,to impress on the mind,.

la:verb:obsequor.gloss: to accommodate oneself to the will of another person; comply with, yield to, gratify, oblige, humor, submit
senses: to accommodate oneself to the will of another person; comply with, yield to, gratify, oblige, humor, submit
to yield to, devote oneself to, give oneself up to or indulge in something
to be yielding, pliant or ductile
la:verb:obsequor.html:
ob-sĕquor, cūtus (quutus), 3, v. dep.
Lit., to accommodate one's self to the will of a person; to comply with, yield to, gratify, humor, submit to; with dat. of the pers. or thing (freq. and class.; syn.: morigeror, obtempero, pareo, oboedio),: cum huic obsecutus sis, illi est repugnandum,; ; : voluntati alicujus,: imperio,. —
With acc. of the thing (ante- and post-class.): et id ego percupio obsequi gnato meo,in this,: ea,.—
Transf.
To yield to, give one's self up to, indulge in a thing: amori,: studiis suis,: fortunae, Caes. ap. : pudori,: tempestati,: est lubido homini suo animo opsequi,: animo,to follow one's inclinations,; : irae,.—
Of inanimate things, to be yielding, pliant, ductile: aes regulare malleis obsequitur,.—Impers. pass.: volo amori obsecutum illius, (v. Lachm. ).—Hence, obsĕ-quens, entis, P. a. (separate, vin' tu te mihi ob esse sequentem an nevis? ).
In gen., yielding, compliant, obsequious: opsequens oboediensque est mori atque inperiis patris,: patri,: legiones nobis,.—Comp.: animus obsequentior,; .— Sup.: curae mortalium obsequentissimam esse Italiam,amenable, susceptible of culture,: nurus,. —
In partic., an appellation of the gods, favorable, indulgent, gracious, propitious: bonam atque obsequentem deam,.—Esp. as subst., of Fortuna: Quem te deum autem nominem? Leo. Fortunam atque obsequentem, ; ; .— Hence, adv.: obsĕquenter, compliantly, obsequiously (perh. not in Cic.): haec a collegā obsequenter facta,: parere alicui,.—Sup.: vixit in contubernio aviae severissime, et tamen obsequentissime,entirely according to her wishes,.

la:verb:obsequere.gloss: second-person singular present active imperative/indicative of obsequor
senses: second-person singular present active imperative/indicative of obsequor

la:verb:obstringo.html:
ob-stringo, strinxi, strictum, 3, v. a.
To bind to or about; to bind, tie, or fasten up (rare): follem obstringit ob gulam,: quom ego Amphitruonem collo hinc obstricto traham,: cervice obstrictā,: tauros aratro,to yoke,.—
To bind, bind up, close up by binding.
Lit. (rare): laqueo collum,. —
Transf.
To shut in, confine: ventos,: viminibus,.—
To hold together by: purpurea vestis ingentibus obstricta gemmis,in which precious stones were the fastenings,.—
Trop., to bind, tie, fetter, hamper; to oblige, lay under obligation (the class. signif. of the word; syn.: obligo, devincio): donis aliquem obstringere,: civitatem jurejurando,: legibus,: foedere,: aliquem aere alieno,to bring into debt,: jurejurando,to bind by an oath,: animam suam,: quam plurimas civitates suo sibi beneficio habere obstrictas volebat,bound, under obligation,: Atticum officiis,: qui se tot sceleribus obstrinxerit,has been guilty of so many crimes,: se parricidio,to commit, perpetrate,: se perjurio,: aliquem conscientiā,to bind by privity, by participation,: obstringi conscientiā tanti sceleris, ne, etc., to be hindered by the sense of so great a crime, from, etc., : aliquem societate scelerum,: fidem suam alicui,to pledge one's word, to promise positively,; ; cf. .—Mid.: qui alienum ... sustulit, furti obstringitur, makes himself guilty, becomes guilty, Sabin. ap. : eidem sceleri obstrictus est,.—Hence, obstrictus, a, um, P. a.; according to III., bound, obliged.—Comp.: obstrictior Debitor,.—Hence, obstrictē, adv.; comp.: obstrictius, more stringently, , 2, 24.

senses: observance, attention, respect, regard, reverence, obedience, deference
la:noun:observantia.html:
observantĭa, ae, f.
observo
,
a remarking, noting, regard, observance.
In gen.: temporum observantia,. —
In partic.
Observance, attention, respect, regard, reverence shown to another: observantia est, per quam aetate, aut sapientiā, aut honore, aut aliquā dignitate antecedentes veremur et colimus,: officia observantiamque dilexit,: tenuiorum,: amicos observantiā, rem parsimoniā retinere,: observantia, quā me colit,: in regem,: eadem pro libertis adversus patronos,.—
An obedient observance; a keeping, following, performing of laws, customs, etc.: prisci moris observantia,: juris,.—
An observance of religious duties, divine worship, religion: fides Catholicae observantiae, Cod. Th. 16, 5, 12, § 54: religio et observantia,.

la:verb:obsolesco.html:
obsŏlesco, lēvi, lētum, 3,
v. inch. n. [obs-olesco], to wear out, to grow old, decay, fall into disuse, lose value, become obsolete

(class.; syn. exolesco): his (verbis) oportet, si possis, non uti: sic enim obsolescent, Müll.: haec ne obsolescerent, renovabam, cum licebat, legendo,: obsolevit jam oratio,: vectigal, quod in bello non obsolescat,: laus,: enituit aliquis in bello, sed obsolevit in pace,.—Hence, obsŏlētus, a, um, P. a.

Lit., old, worn out, thrown off: erat veste obsoletā,: vestitus,: amiculum,: vestitu obsoletiore, Cig. Agr. 2, 5, 13: homo obsoletus,in a worn-out dress,: tectum,old, ruinous,: verba,obsolete,: obsoleta et vulgaria,.—
Transf., common, ordinary, poor, mean, low: crimina,: gaudia,.—Comp.: obsoletior oratio,a too ordinary, too negligent style,: honores,of little worth,: color,: o nec paternis obsoleta sordibus,: dextra obsoleta sanguine,defiled,.—Hence, adv.: obsŏlētē, in an old or worn-out style, poorly, meanly: paulo tamen obsoletius vestitus,.

senses: to besiege; hem in, beset, invest, blockade a place
to watch closely; to be on the lookout for
la:verb:obsideo.html:
ob-sĭdĕo, ēdi, essum, 2, v. n. and a.
[sedeo].
Neutr., to sit, stay, remain, abide anywhere (only poet.): servi ne obsideant, liberis ut sit locus,: domi obsidere,: in limine,.—
Act., to sit at, on, or in, to remain on or in, to haunt, inhabit, frequent a place.
In gen.: aram,: ranae stagna et rivos obsident,frequent marshes,: obsedit limina bubo,: Apollo umbilicum terrarum obsidet,.—
In partic.
Milit. t. t., to sit down before, to hem in, beset, besiege, invest, blockade a place (cf. oppugno): cum omnes aditus armati obsiderent,: Curio Uticam obsidere instituit,: consiliis ab oppugnandā urbe ad obsidendam versis,: propius inopiam erant obsidentes quam obsessi,: ut Carthaginem crederent extemplo Scipionem obsessurum,: totam Italiam,: vias,: vallis obsessa,: egregias Lateranorum aedīs,.—
To occupy, fill, possess: corporibus omnis obsidetur locus,is filled,: senatum armis,: palus obsessa salictis,full of osier-thickets,: Trachasque obsessa palude,i. e. surrounded,.—
Trop., to occupy, possess, take possession of: alicujus animum,: qui meum tempus obsideret,who took up my time,; : cum obsideri aures a fratre cerneret,that they were continually besieged by his brother,—
To have one's eye upon, to watch closely, be on the look-out for: jacere humi ... ad obsidendum stuprum,: rostra,.
la:verb:obsideo.inflection: ēdi, essum, 2, v. n. and a.

la:verb:obscuro.html:
obscūro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
id.
,
to render dark, to darken, obscure (class.; syn.: obumbro, opaco).
Lit.: obscuratur et offunditur luce solis lumen lucernae,: nitor solis,: finitimas regiones eruptione Aetnaeorum ignium,: caelum nocte atque nubibus obscuratum,: volucres Aethera obscurant pennis,: nebula caelum obscurabat, ap. : obscuratus sol, obscured,

eclipsed, ; ; ; ; ; , ext. 1: visus obscuratus,dimmed eyesight,.—

Transf., to hide, conceal, cover; to render invisible or imperceptible: neque nox tenebris obscurare coetus nefarios potest,: caput obscurante lacernā,: caput dextra,: dolo ipsi et signa militaria obscurati,concealed, kept out of sight,: nummus in Croesi divitiis obscuratur,disappears, is lost,: tenebrae non obscurabuntur a te,.—
Trop.
To blind, darken, becloud the understanding: scio amorem tibi Pectus obscurasse,.—
Of speech, to obscure, render indistinct; to deliver or express indistinctly: si erunt mihi plura ad te scribenda, ἀλληγορίαις obscurabo, : nihil dicendo,: aliquid callide,; cf. : stilum affectatione,to render obscure,.—
Of sound, to pronounce indistinctly: (M) neque eximitur sed obscuratur,is pronounced indistinctly,: vocem, to render dull or indistinct, .—
To obscure, cover with obscurity; to render unknown: paupertas quorum obscurat nomina, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 73 Vahl.): fortuna res cunctas ex lubidine magis, quam ex vero celebrat obscuratque,.—
(Acc. to I. B.) To suppress, hide, conceal: quod obscurari non potest,: laudes,: veritatem,.—Hence, to obscure, cause to be forgotten, render of no account: magnitudo lucri obscurabat periculi magnitudinem,.—In pass.: obscurari, to become obscure or of no account, to grow obsolete, etc.: sin dicit obscurari quaedam nec apparere, quia valde parva sint, nos quoque concedimus,: omnis eorum memoria sensim obscurata est et evanuit,; cf. id. Fragm. ap. : obscurata vocabula,obsolete,.

la:noun:obsequium.gloss: complaisance, yielding, compliance, obedience; allegiance; deference, obsequiousness, flattery
senses: complaisance, yielding, compliance, obedience; allegiance; deference, obsequiousness, flattery
la:noun:obsequium.html:
ob-sĕquĭum, ii, n.
obsequor
.
In gen., compliance, yieldingness, complaisance, indulgence (class.; syn.: indulgentia, obsequentia): prosequium a prosequendo, obsequium ab obsequendo dicuntur, Paul. ex Müll.: obsequium amicos, veritas odium parit,: obsequium atque patientia,: obsequium et comitas,: alicui tribuere,: ventris,i. e. gluttony,: animo sumere,to follow the bent of one's inclinations,: in obsequio uxoris,in the service of his wife,.—Of inanim. things: flectitur obsequio curvatus ab arbore ramus,by yielding, by its pliancy,.—In plur.: omnia ei obsequia polliceor, Planc. ap. .—
In partic.
Compliance in love, yielding, consent, ; ; ; .—
Obedience, allegiance: in populum Romanum,: principum,i. e. towards them,: ad obsequium redigere,to subjugate,: nulla colonia vestra erit, quae nos obsequio erga vos fideque superet,: obsequium in regem retinere, (43) fin.; 13, 3; : jurare in obsequium alicujus, to swear obedience or allegiance to one, : obsequium erga aliquem exuere,to throw off,.

la:noun:obsonium.html:
obsōnĭum or ops-, ii, n., = ὀψώνιον,
that which is eaten with bread; victuals, viands, esp. fish: tu facito obsonatum nobis sit opulentum obsonium,: curare,: obsonare,: scindere,; : coëmere,: opsonia rancidula,.—Also of fruit, .

senses: repulsive, offensive, abominable, hateful, disgusting, filthy
la:adj:obscenus.html:
obscēnus (obscaen-, and less properly obscoen-), a, um, adj.
perh. ob and caenum, filth
,
of adverse, unfavorable, evil omen; ill-boding, inauspicious, ominous, portentous (cf.: sinister, funestus): apud antiquos omnes fere obscena dicta sunt, quae mali ominis habebantur, Paul. ex Müll.: obsceni interpres funestique ominis auctor, Matius ap. Müll.; Att. ap. : deūm rixa vertat verba obscena,; Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 182 Vahl.): montem istum (Aventinum) excluserunt, quasi avibus obscenis ominosum (viz., by reason of the birds, which gave unfavorable omens to Remus), Mess. ap. ; so, volucres, birds of illomen, i. e. owls, : canes,: obscenum ostentum,: omen,: puppis, the fatal ship, that bore Helen when she eloped with Paris to Troy, ; cf.: Troja,: anus,old witches, hags,.—Sup.: Alliesis dies dicebatur apud Romanos obscenissimi ominis, Paul. ex Fest. s. v. Alliesis, p. 7 Müll.—
Transf., repulsive, offensive, abominable, hateful, disgusting, filthy.
In gen. (poet. and in post-Aug. prose; syn.: immundus, turpis): (Allecto) frontem obscenam rugis arat,: volucres pelagi,i. e. the harpies,; 262: upupa, obscena alias pastu avis,; cf. fames, : haustus,of filthy water,: cruor,.— As subst.: obscēna, ōrum, n., the excrements, ; also, the urine: qui clam latuit reddente obscena puellā,; cf. .—
In partic., offensive to modesty, i. e. immodest, impure, indecent, lewd, obscene (class.; syn.: spurcus, impurus): delicatae et obscenae voluptates,: adulterium,: obscenas tabellas pingere, (6, 27): carmina,: gestus motusque,: obscenum in modum formata commotaque manus,i. e. so as to suggest impure thoughts,: jocandi genus flagitiosum, obscenum,: si obscena nudis nominibus enuntientur,: quodque facere turpe non est, modo occulte, id dicere obscenum est,; cf. § 128; . —Comp.: illud Antipatri paulo obscenius,: abjectior et obscenior vita,fin.—Sup.: obscenissimi versus,; .—
Subst.
obscēnus, i, m., a lewd person: quis enim non vicus abundat Tristibus obscenis,.—
obscēna, ōrum, less freq. in the sing., obscēnum, i. n., the private parts, τὰ αἰδοῖα.—Plur.: Nymphe fugiens obscena Priapi,; cf.: pars nudi agunt, pars tantum obscena velati,: obscena,; : obscena corporis,.—Sing.: virile,; ; ; Jul. Obsequ. 84.—Hence, also, adv.: obscēnē (acc. to II. B), impurely, indecently, lewdly, obscenely (class.): latrocinari, fraudare, adulterare, re turpe est, sed dicitur non obscene,.—Comp.: cujus (Mercurii) obscenius excitata natura traditur,: obscenius concurrerent litterae,.—Sup.: impudicissime et obscenissime vixit,.

la:noun:obscenitas.html:
obscēnĭtas (obscaen-, obscoen-), ātis, f.
obscenus
. *
Unfavorableness, inauspiciousness, of a bad omen: mali ominis obscenitas,.—
Moral impurity, foulness, unchastity, lewdness, obscenity.
In abstr. (the class. signif. of the word): si rerum turpitudo adhibetur et verborum obscenitas,; cf. ; cf. also : si quod sit in obscenitate flagitium, id aut in re esse aut in verbo,: obscenitas non a verbis tantum abesse debet, sed etiam a significatione,: eques Romanus obscenitatis in feminas reus,: professis apud se obscenitatem cetera quoque concessisse delicta,unchastity,: obscenitate oris hirsuto atque olido seni clare exprobrata,the disfigurement produced by lewdness,: in obscenitatem, aliquem compellere,.—
Concr., an obscene thing (post-Aug. and very rare): corporum obscenitas, = τὰ αἰδοῖα, : amputata,.— Plur.: in poculis libidines caelare juvit ac per obscenitates bibere,obscene figures, prooem. § 5.

la:adv:obscene.gloss: obscenely, so as to involve obscenity (of language), indecently, lewdly

la:noun:obsidio.html:
obsĭdĭo, ōnis, f.
obsideo
.
Lit.
In gen., a siege, investment, blockade of a place (class.): obsidionem potias dicendum esse, quam obsidium, adjuvat nos testimonio suo Ennius in Telamone, Paul. ex Müll.; v. Müll. ad loc.; and cf.: cui tu obsidionem paras, Enn. ib. (Trag. v. 365 Vahl.); and: obsidionem obducere,: partim vi, partim obsidione urbes capere,: aliquem in obsidione habere,: cum spes major Romanis in obsidione quam in oppugnatione esset,: obsidione eximere, to free or relcase from, : obsidione cingere,to besiege, blockade,; : obsidionem tolerare,to stand,: obsidionem exsequi,to carry on,: obsidionem omittere,to raise,: obsidionem solvere, to put an end to a siege, by either surrender or relief: tolerando paucos dies totam soluturos obsidionem,; cf. : solutā obsidione,raised,; : eam obsidionem sine certamine adveniens Cn. Scipio solvit,; ; ; ; ; : liberare obsidionem, to raise the siege: non ad Romam obsidendam, sed ad Capuae liberandam obsidionem Hannibalem ire,; cf. obsidium fin.: longae dira obsidionis egestas,. —
Transf., captivity (post-class.), ; ; .—
Trop., pressing, imminent danger: obsidione rem publicam liberare,: feneratores ex obsidione eximere,to free from the danger of losing their money,; ; cf. obsidium.

la:noun:obses.gloss: hostage (a person given as a pledge or security for the performance of the conditions of a treaty or similar agreement, such as to ensure the status of a vassal)
senses: hostage (a person given as a pledge or security for the performance of the conditions of a treaty or similar agreement, such as to ensure the status of a vassal)
la:noun:obses.html:
obses (old orthogr. opses, in the first Epit. of the Scipios;
v.infra; Inscr. Spec. Epigr. p. 5, 11 Jahn), ĭdis (gen. plur. obsidium, ; ; ), m. and f.
ob-sedeo
.
Lit., a hostage: OPSIDES ABDOVCIT, first Epit. of the Scipios: ut obsides accipere, non dare consueverint,; : obsides alicui imperare,: dedere,: retinere aliquem obsidem,as a hostage,.—Fem.: me tamen acceptā poterat deponere bellum Obside,: obsides, qui Porsenae mittebantur,: inter se dare,to exchange,.—

Transf., in gen., a surety, security, bail, pledge (syn.: sponsor, vindex, vas, praes): Phocion se ejus rei obsidem fore, pollicitus est,to be surety, to answer for it,: accipere aliquem obsidem nuptiarum,: conjugii,: rei,: dare obsides, with a foll. acc. and inf., to give a surety or guarantee: tantum modo oratoribus Metellus obsides non dedit, se nullā in re Verri similem futurum,.—Also of inanim. subjects: habemus a C. Caesare sententiam tamquam obsidem perpetuae in rem publicam voluntatis,; ; ; : obsidem enim se animum ejus habere,.

la:verb:obsido.html:
ob-sīdo, ĕre,
v. a., to beset, invest, besiege, blockade (mostly poet.): ne auriculam obsidat caries, ne vermiculique, Lucil. ap. : vias oculorum,: certas partes,: pontem, Kritz N. cr.: portas,: Italos fines,to occupy, take possession of,: praedator cupit immensos obsidere campos,: Troica moenia,.

la:noun:obsessio.html:
obsessĭo, ōnis, f.
obsideo
,
a blocking up, besieging, encompassing, a blockade of a place (class.): obsessio templorum,: militaris viae,: castrorum,: obsessionem alicuius omittere,

la:verb:obstipesco.html:
ob-stĭpesco and ob-stŭpesco, pŭi, 3,
v. inch. n. and a., to become senseless, lose feeling; to be stupefied, benumbed (syn.: obtorpesco; class.).
Lit.: apes obstupescunt potantes,: corpus,.—
Trop., to be astonished, astounded, amazed, to be struck with amazement: quid hic, malum, adstans obstipuisti,: ob haec beneficia, quibus illi obstupescunt,: ejus aspectu cum obstupuisset bubulcus,: visu Aeneas,: obstupuerunt stupore magno, et saep.—
With acc., to wonder or be astonished at any thing (post-class.), .

la:verb:obsto.gloss: to stand before, stand in the way of, obstruct, block, oppose
senses: to stand before, stand in the way of, obstruct, block, oppose
la:verb:obsto.html:
ob-sto, stĭti, ātum (obstaturus, ; ; ;
gen. plur. obstantum, ), 1, v. n., to stand before or against any thing.
In gen. (very rare): soli luna obstitit, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 167 Vahl.); cf.: montibus obstipis obstantibus, id. ap. Paul. ex Müll. (Ann. v. 407 ib.): dominae niveis a vultibus obstas,; so, summis a postibus,: obviam,to stand in the way,.—
In partic., to stand against or in the way of a person or thing; to withstand, thwart, hinder, oppose, obstruct (the class. signif. of the word; syn.: obsisto, adversor, officio).—Constr. with dat., absol., with quin, quominus, cur, or ne.
With dat.: quae tardis mora noctibus obstet,: alicui,: cur

mihi te offers ac meis commodis officis et obstas? ; cf. : vita cetera eorum huic sceleri obstat,their former life stands opposed to this crime, secures them against the suspicion of this crime,: di omnes quibus obstitit Ilium,was an offence to,: nam sic labentibus (aedibus) obstat vilicus,i. e. keeps from falling,; cf. v. 243.—For the dat. in with acc. is found: in laudem vetustorum invidia non obstat,.—

Absol.: me obstare, illos obsequi, Enn. ap. : restitant, occurrunt, obstant, id. ap. (Sat. v. 5 ib.): obstando magis quam pugnando castra tutabantur, 25: exercitus hostium duo obstant,block up the way,; : si omnia removentur, quae obstant et impediunt,.—
With quin: quibus non humana ulla, neque divina obstant, quin socios amicos trahant, exscindant, Dietsch.—
With quominus: quid obstat, quominus sit beatus?: ne quid divini humanive obstet, quominus justum piumque de integro ineatur bellum,.—(ε) With cur: quid obstat, cur non (verae nuptiae) fiant?.— (ζ) With ne: Histiaeus Milesius, ne res conficeretur, obstitit,: cum ibi quoque religio obstaret, ne non posset nisi ab consule dici dictator,: ne id, quod placebat, decerneret in tantae nobilitatis viris, ambitio obstabat,.—
Impers. pass.: nec, si non obstatur, propterea etiam permittitur,: indignatur amans Obstari animae,.—
Part. pres. in plur. as subst.: obstantia, ĭum, n.: obstantia silvarum amoliri,hinderances, obstructions,.

la:verb:obstruo.gloss: to build before or against; build, block, or wall up; stop up, barricade, render impassable
senses: to build before or against; build, block, or wall up; stop up, barricade, render impassable
to obstruct, stop up, hinder, impede
la:verb:obstruo.html:
ob-strŭo (opstr-), xi, ctum, 3,
v. a., to build before or against; to build, block, or wall up; to stop up, barricade, renderimpassable (class.; cf. obsaepio, claudo, oppilo).
Lit.: validum pro diruto obstruentes murum,: frontem castrorum auxiliis,.—Esp., to build before so as to obstruct the light: obstructae fenestrae,: FENESTRAS OPSTRVITO, Lex. Puteol. ap. Grut. 207, 2: luminibus alicujus,: jus luminum obstruendorum redimere, to purchase permission of a neighbor to build so as to obstruct his light, Inscr. Guarin. Comment. in Vet. Monument. 1, p. 64: portas,: valvas aedis. : aditus,: flumina,: aquarum venas,: saxa,placed in the way,: cujus aures morbus obstruxit,has stopped up, made deaf,: os obstruere,to close the mouth, to make silent,; .—
Trop., to stop up, hinder, impede, obstruct: Catonis luminibus obstruxit haec posteriorum quasi exaggerata altius oratio,was a hinderance to,: viri deus obstruit aures,stops, renders deaf, inexorable,: perfugia improborum,shuts off,: cognitionem difficultatibus,to impede, obstruct,: mentes,.—
Intr., to be in the way: si officiens signis mons obstruet altus,.

la:verb:obsisto.html:
ob-sisto, stĭti, stĭtum, 3,
v. n., to set, place, or post one's self before any thing (class.; syn.: adversor, repugno).
In gen.: hic obsistam, ne, etc.,will station myself,: alicui obviam,to plant one's self in another's way,: obsistens obtestansque,: plures abeunti Volumnio obsistere,.—
In partic.
To set one's self against; to oppose, resist, withstand: qui cum obsistere ac defendere conarentur,: omnibus ejus consiliis,: dolori,: odiis,: vitiis,: visis,to disapprove of,: opinionibus,. —With inf.: obstitit Oceanus in se simul atque in Herculem inquiri,opposes, forbids,.—With ne: Histiaeus Miletus ne res conficeretur obstitit,: obstitisti, ne ex Italiā transire in Siciliam fugitivorum copiae possent,.—With quominus: quae si cui obstitit, quominus referret gratiam, etc.,.—Impers. pass.: magnitudine animi facile posset repugnari obsistique fortunae,.—
obstĭ-tus, a, um, P. a.
Over against, opposite: luna radios solis obstiti vel adversi usurpat,.—
Lit., opposing, inimical; hence, in augury, struck by lightning: obstitum Cloatius et Aelius Stilo esse aiunt violatum attactumque de caelo. Cincius quom qui deo deaeque obstiterit id est qui viderit, quod videri nefas esset, Paul. ex Müll.: FVLGVRA ATQVE OBSTITA PIANTO,.

la:verb:obsero.html:
obsĕro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
ob-sera
,
to bolt, bar, fasten, or shut up (not in Cic. or Cæs.; syn.: claudo, oppilo, obstruo).
Lit.: ostium,: aedificia,: fores (opp. aperire),: tabellam liminis,: exitus,: rogos,i. e. the dead,.—
Transf.: aures,: palatum (for os), i. e. to be silent, : fores amicitiae,.

la:verb:obsero#2.gloss: to sow thickly, to cover with seeds

la:verb:obsero#2.html:
obsĕro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
ob-sera
,
to bolt, bar, fasten, or shut up (not in Cic. or Cæs.; syn.: claudo, oppilo, obstruo).
Lit.: ostium,: aedificia,: fores (opp. aperire),: tabellam liminis,: exitus,: rogos,i. e. the dead,.—
Transf.: aures,: palatum (for os), i. e. to be silent, : fores amicitiae,.

la:noun:observatio.html:
observātĭo, ōnis, f.
observo
,
a watching, observing, observance (class.).
In gen.: observationi operam dare,: siderum,.—As a gift or faculty, the power of observation, .—
In partic.
An office, duty, service (eccl. Lat.): Dei sui et expiationis, Esdr. 12, 44: in observationibus sicut fas est,.—
An observation, remark; a precept, rule (post-Aug.), : dare observationes aliquas coquendi,: sermonis antiqui,.—
In partic., circumspection, care, exactness: summa erat observatio in bello movendo,.—
Regard, respect, esteem, reverence (post-class.): religionibus suam observationem reddere,: Christianitatis, Cod. Th. 12, 1, 112: divina,.—
Display, outward show (eccl. Lat.): non venit regnum Dei cum observatione,.—
Observance: dierum,.

la:noun:obscuritas.html:
obscūrĭtas, ātis, f.
obscurus
,
a being dark, darkness, obscurity.
Lit. (perh. only post-Aug.): latebrarum,: atra,: visūs,dimness,: oculorum,. —
Trop. (class.), obscurity, indistinctness, uncertainty: ut oratio, quae lumen adhibere rebus debet, ea obscuritatem et tenebras afferat,: Pythagorae,: obscuritas fit etiam vet is ab usu remotis,: in eā obscuritate ac dubitatione omnium,uncertainty,: rerum,: naturae,.—In plur.: quo pertinent obscuritates et aenigmata somniorum,: obscuritates non adsignemus culpae scribentium, sed inscientiae non adsequentium, Caecil. ap. : obscuritatibus involutum,.—
Of rank, obscurity, lowliness, meanness: quorum prima aetas propter humilitatem et obscuritatem, in hominum ignoratione versatur. : sordes et obscuritatem Vitellianarum partium perstringemus,: generis,: nec obscuritas inhibuit (Servium Tullium), quamvis matre servā creatum,.

la:noun:obsecratio.html:
obsĕcrātĭo, ōnis, f.
obsecro
.
In gen., a beseeching, imploring, supplication, entreaty (class.): prece et obsecratione humili uti,; : judicum,addressed to the judges,: percipe obsecrationem meam,: fit ad Deum pro illis,.—
In partic.
An asseveration, protestation, accompanied by an invocation of the gods or of religious things, Gr. δέησις, ; cf. ; cf. .—
A public prayer: obsecrationem indicere,; ; ; ; : habere,.

la:noun:obstetrix.html:
obstē^trix (opst-) or obstī^trix (opst-), īcis, f.
obsto
,
a midwife: peperit Sine obstetricis operā,; : mittere ad obstetricem,; ; : obstetricum nobilitas,;

la:noun:obsequiae.html:
obsĕquĭae, ārum, f.
obsequor
, for exsequiae,
funeral rites, obsequies, , n. 235 (Burm. and Meyer read exsequias).

la:noun:obstaculum.html:
ob-stācŭlum, i, n.
obsto
,
a hinderance, obstacle (post-class.; cf. impedimentum): teneris et rarioribus parcit (fulmen), quia transitu patente minus obstaculum invenit,: rumpere obstacula,; ; ; .—In plur., of mountains, .

la:noun:obscuratio.html:
obscūrātĭo, ōnis, f.
obscuro
,
a darkening, obscuring, obscuration (class.).
Lit.: solis, ap. , 5, 15; ; : in illā obscuratione, darkness, obscurity, Auct. B. Hisp. 6.—
Trop.: in quibus (voluptatibus) propter earum exiguitatem, obscuratio consequitur,an obscuring, a rendering invisible,; cf. ; cf. obscuro.

la:verb:obstetrico.gloss: to perform the office of a midwife, assist at childbirth
senses: to perform the office of a midwife, assist at childbirth
la:verb:obstetrico.html:
obstē^trīco (opst-), āre, v. n. and a.
[id.], to perform the office of a midwife (eccl. Lat.), : Hebraeas (sc. mulieres),to assist in childbirth,: obstetricandi scientia,.—
Trop.: poëtis obstetricantibus,.

la:noun:obstinatio.html:
obstĭnātĭo, ōnis, f.
obstino
,
firmness, in a good and bad sense; resolution, steadfastness, determination, inflexibility, stubbornness, obstinacy (class.; syn.: pertinacia, contumacia): quae ego omnia obstinatione sententiae repudiavi,out of adherence to my principles,: animi,: fidei,: taciturna,obstinate silence,: inflexibilis,.—In plur., .

la:verb:observo#2.html:
ob-servo, āvi, ātum, 1 (archaic
fut. perf. observasso, ), v. a.
In gen., to watch, note, heed, observe a thing; to take notice of, pay attention to (class.; syn.: animadverto, attendo): ne me observare possis, quid rerum geram,: quid ille faciat, ne id observes,: fetus,to watch for, seek to catch,: lupus observavit, dum dormitarent canes,watched, waited,: occupationem alicujus, et aucupari tempus,to watch in order to take advantage of,: si iniquitates observaveris, Domine,: tempus epistulae alicui reddendae, to watch or wait for, : et insidiari,to be on the watch,: observavit sedulo, ut praetor indiceret, etc., took care that, etc., .—So pass. impers.: observatum est, ne quotiens introiret urbem, supplicium de quoquam sumeretur,: observans Acerroniae necem,observing, perceiving,: postquam poëta sensit, scripturam suam Ab iniquis observari,to be scrutinized,: sese,to keep a close watch over one's self,.—
In partic.
To watch, guard, keep any thing: januam,: fores,: greges,: draconem, auriferam obtutu observantem arborem, Poët. ap. ; .—
To observe, respect, regard, attend to, heed, keep, comply with a law, precept, recommendation, etc.: leges,: censoriam animadversionem,: praeceptum diligentissime,: imperium,: foedus,: centesimas,to adhere to,: commendationes,to attend to, regard,: auspicia,: diem concilii,: ordines,to keep in the ranks,.—Pass.: id ab omnibus,.—
To pay attention or respect to; to respect, regard, esteem, honor one (syn.: veneror, revereor): tribules suos,: regem,: me, ut alterum patrem, et observat, et diligit,: et colere aliquem,: aliquem perofficiose et amanter,: clarissimus et nobis observandus vir,.—
Observare se a quā re = se abstinere, .—
To observe, notice, perceive (eccl. Lat.): Amasa non observavit gladium,.—Hence,
ob-servans, antis, P. a.
Watchful, regardful, observant.—Comp.: observantior aequi Fit populus,.—Sup.: observantissimus omnium officiorum,; : observantissima lex suorum itinerum, App. de Mundo, 33 fin.—
Attentive, respectful: homo tui observans,; P.: observantissimus mei homo,; —Hence, adv.: observanter, carefully, sedulously (post-class.): sequi,; .—Comp.: observantius,.—Sup.: aliquid observantissime vitare,.—
Reverentially: ad precandum accedere,.—
observātē, adv., observantly, carefully, perspicaciously (postclass.): observate curioseque animadvertit M. Tullius,.

la:verb:obstino.gloss: to resolve, determine, be firmly resolved, persist
senses: to resolve, determine, be firmly resolved, persist
la:verb:obstino.html:
obstĭno, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
a lengthened form of obsto
,
to set about a thing with firmness or resolution, to set one's mind firmly on, to persist in, be resolved on a thing (as a verb. fin. very rare; only the Part. as a P. a. is freq.).
With acc.: id inhiat, ea affinitatem hanc obstinavit gratia,.—Pass.: obstinari exorsus, Pac. ap. Paul. ex Müll. (Trag. Rel. p. 425 Rib.).—
With inf.: obstinaverant animis aut vincere, aut mori,.—
Absol.: ipso Vespasiano inter initia imperii ad obtinendas iniquitates haud perinde obstinante,.— Hence, obstĭnātus, a, um, P. a., firmly set, fixed, resolved, in a good or bad sense; determined, resolute, steadfast, inflexible, stubborn, obstinate (class.; syn.: pervicax, pertinax): vos qui astatis obstinati, Naev. ap. Paul. ex Müll. (Trag. Rel. p. 11 Rib.): obstinato animo aliquid facere, Att. ap. Paul. ex Fest. l. l. (Trag. Rel. p. 123 Rib.); so,: ad decertandum obstinati animi,: ad silendum,: ad mortem, : adversus lacrimas,; : ad resistendum,: contra veritatem,: pudicitia,: fides,: aures,.—With inf.: jam obstinatis mori spes affulsit,; ; : obstinatum est tibi, non suscipere imperium, nisi, etc.,you are firmly resolved,.—Rarely with in: obstinatae in perniciem Romae urbes,: in extrema,: militum animos obstinatos pro Vitellio subruere,.—Comp.: voluntas obstinatior,: adversus lacrimas muliebres,firmer, more steadfast,.—Sup.: virtus obstinatissima,the most resolute,: rex obstinatissimus,.—Hence, adv.: obstĭ-nātē, firmly, inflexibly, in a good and bad sense; resolutely, pertinaciously, stubbornly, obstinately (class.): ita me obstinate aggressus, ut, etc.,: operam dat,: negari,: magis ac magis induruisse,.—Comp.: obstinatius omnia agere,.—Sup.: obstinatissime recusare,.

la:verb:obstrepo.gloss: to roar or resound at; resound, sound
senses: to roar or resound at; resound, sound
to clamor or cry out against; blame
to be troublesome to; annoy; impede, hinder
to fill with noise, cause to resound
la:verb:obstrepo.html:
ob-strĕpo, ŭi, ĭtum, 3, v. n. and a.
Neutr.
Prop., to make a noise against or at; to roar or resound at; to resound, sound.—With dat.: marisque Baiis obstrepentis urges Submovere litora,: remotis Obstrepit Oceanus Britannis,: multaque nativis obstrepit arbor aquis,si, intrante te, clamor, et plausus, et pantomimica ornamenta obstrepuerint, si, etc.,: fontesque lymphis obstrepunt manantibus,: tympana ... raucis Obstrepuere sonis,: garrula per ramos avis obstrepit,sings aloud,: jam genus totum obstrepit,makes loud lament,.—Impers., there is a noise, a noise arises: non statim, si quid obstrepet, abiciendi codices erunt, etc.,if there shall be a noise,.—
Trop.
To bawl or shout against; to clamor or cry out against.
Absol.: adversarius obstrepit,.—
With dat.: certatim alter alteri obstrepere,: ut quodammodo ipsi sibi in dicendo obstrepere videantur,.—
Impers. pass.: decemviro obstrepitur,.—
To annoy, molest, be troublesome to.—With dat.: quae res fecit, ut tibi litteris obstrepere non auderem,.—
To impede or hinder; to prove an obstacle, hinderance, or injury to.
With dat.: detrectare Pompeium, actisque ejus obstrepere,: remove parentem, ne tuae laudi obstrepat,.—
Absol.: nihil sensere (Poeni), obstrepente pluviā,: ut accipiatur circumjecto candore lux, et, temperato repercussu, non obstrepat,: scelerati, conscientiā obstrepente, condormire non possunt, : sed clausae sunt aures, obstrepente irā,.—
To cry out against, blame.—With dat.: huic definitioni ita obstrepunt,.—
Act., to clamor against; to oppose, disturb: tamen ejus modi, etiam cum leguntur, obstrepi clamore militum videntur, et tubarum sono,: quae in Cn. Pompeium congesta sunt: hinc assensione favoris, illinc fremitu invidiae, litterarum monumentis obstrepuntur,are perverted, distorted,.—
To fill with noise, cause to resound: secretus ab omni voce locus, si non opstreperetur aquis,.

obstīpus, a, um, adj.
ob-stipes
,
bent or inclined to one side; opp. to rectus (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
In gen., oblique, shelving: omnia mendose fieri atque obstipa, necesse est,. 517: obstitum (leg. obstipum) obliquum, Enn. Libr. XVI.: montibus obstitis (leg. obstipis) obstantibus, unde oritur nox. Et in Libr. VIII.: amplius exaugere obstipolumve (leg. opstipo lumine) solis. Caecilius in imbros (leg. Imbris): resupina obstito (leg. obstipo) capitulo sibi ventum facere cunicula (leg. tunicula). Lucretius: omnia, etc.; v.supra, Paul. ex Müll.; v. Müll. ad loc.; and cf. and 407 Vahl.; and Trag. Rel. p. 44 Rib.—
Esp.
Bent or drawn back, said of the stiff neck of a proud person: cervix rigida et obstipa,.—
Bent forward, bent or bowed down: stes capite obstipo, multum similis metuenti,.—So of one lost in thought: obstipo capite et figentes lumine terram,.—
Bent or inclined to one side, of the dragon's head, a translation of the Gr. λοξὸν κάρη: obstipum caput et tereti cervice reflexum,; cf. .—
Transf., stiff - necked, obstinate, perverse (eccl. Lat.), Jul. ap. Aug. c. Sec. Resp. Jul. 3, 38.—Hence, obstīpē, adv., perversely, Jul. ap. Aug. c. Sec. Resp. Jul. 6, 25.
